_note: EXAMPLE lead, committed so the /next route stays buildable and reviewable on a fresh clone. Every family-identifying value here is a placeholder. Real lead files are gitignored: this repository is public and a real file carries a minor's first name, a parent's email and a phone number. Copy this file to app/next/leads/<lead>-<6 hex>.json, fill it from the lead's own record, and leave it out of git. Firm-side copy below (pamphlet sentences, the price ladder and the stats) is what the pamphlets already print and is safe to keep.
_idNote: Stored on the lead_pages row and on the calendar event (extendedProperties.leadId), so it must stay stable and lowercase-hyphen. The SLUG is the file name; the id is the analytics handle.
_modeNote: TWO PAGES, ONE ROUTE (2026-09-07 evening, Ryan via Aaron). "heavy" (or absent, or null): the page renders the calendar, the sticky Pick a time bar and the second-conversation stages, which is what Conor's live row does and what this key must never change. "light": the booking block, the sticky bar and the anchor are all gone, /api/next/slots and /api/next/book refuse the slug outright, and in the calendar's place sits one raised panel whose only action is the subject-only mailto built from `interest` below. Ryan's words: "light version: after the first initial, they get a stripped-down version of the pamphlet that has NO pricing in the /lead; if you're interested, let us know so we can move on to the next stage." His reason for withholding the calendar, verbatim: "if light gets access to the calendar, everyone will book for a free 30 min even if they have NO intention of signing up." So a light row's `booking` object is still filled in and simply unread, the way clockFallback is: escalating a family to the heavy page is one key and one re-seed, not a rewrite. A light row's `next.lines` must also be written to the light beats (read the brochures, tell us if you want options, Ryan puts them together himself); the page does not police the copy, and stage language about a second conversation on a page that offers no time is the one failure this mode can still ship.
_interestNote: The light page's CTA, and read only when mode is "light". Every field is optional and page.js carries a working default for each: `heading` (an H2, its last word set in italic terracotta by the page, so end it on a word worth accenting), `sub` (one line under it, omitted entirely when absent), `panel` (the one sentence inside the raised block), `buttonLabel`, and the mailto's `to` and `subject`. THERE IS NO BODY FIELD, deliberately: a prefilled body puts words in a parent's mouth and is then sent verbatim, which reads as a form response to whoever opens it. A subject line is a yes, and that is all this button has to carry. THE ADDRESS DEFAULTS TO ryan@ryanchoice.com, not ryan@admissions.partners: the second is an alias of support@ and nothing watches it as a lead inbox. The subject names the student's first name and nothing else about the family, because it travels through whatever hop their mail takes. The address is also printed as visible text under the button, for a family reading mail in a browser tab where a mailto opens nothing.
_studentNote: First name only, and only if that is genuinely all we have. Never guess a surname from a filing handle: print the name the family gave, and print nothing where they gave nothing.
opening: Looking forward to talking again. This page is for you and your parents: what I heard, what happens next, and a place to pick a time.

heard.body: One sentence, in Ryan's read, with no claim attached to it.
Your main interest. With us it is true mentorship from ideation to finalization, with weekly meetings and detailed feedback every step of the way.
One sentence naming the systems in play, and nothing about deadlines.
Cut the line if there is no fourth thing. Four is not a quota.

_heardNote: Only things Ryan actually said. No inferred interest, no claim about a placement, a program or an organisation that has not agreed to anything.
_videoNote: Ryan films one per segment later. Null renders nothing at all, not an empty frame.
clockTail: Ryan's late afternoon is your next morning, which is where meetings sit.
_clockNote: The live line is COMPUTED in the browser from the two zones, never typed, because a typed clock is wrong within the hour. Singapore is UTC+8 with no daylight saving; Irvine follows America/Los_Angeles, which does observe it, so the offset is 15 hours now and 16 in the winter. The fallback string is what a reader with scripting off sees, and it is the only place a number is hard-coded; it is correct until US clocks change on 2026-11-01.

booking.heading: Pick a time.
booking.sub: Thirty minutes on Zoom with Ryan. Every time below is on your own clock.
booking.zoneNote: Friday evening in California is Saturday morning in Singapore.
booking.emptyLabel: No mornings are open in the next two weeks. Email us and we will find one.
booking._subNote: The chips stopped carrying Ryan's clock on 2026-09-04, so this sentence stopped promising it. Both clocks still appear on the confirm sentence, which is where the family commits.

_bookingNote: The page books Ryan's real calendar through the portal's own engine; it does NOT punt to Calendly, and there is no Calendly link, embed or UTM anywhere in this flow. Slots come from the same availability code app/api/getAvailableSlots serves students from, so a family is never offered a time the booking gate would refuse. NOTHING IS HELD: the offer is computed live at render and re-verified live at confirm, because a pre-reserved slot is a meeting Ryan cannot see and nothing ever releases it. `morning` is the family's own clock, 07:00 to 11:00: Ryan's standing hours (Tue-Thu 16-20, Fri 16-19 Pacific) already land entirely inside a Singapore morning, so his ordinary availability IS the offer and no special arrangement is needed. `calendarName` is the internal filing handle Ryan reads in his own day, deliberately different from the greeting name the page addresses the student by. Attribution rides on the row and the calendar event (leadSlug), which is what replaced the UTMs.

proof.essay: When my mentor suggested rerouting a section of my PCB to reduce crosstalk, I initially felt defensive; however, once I implemented the change, the signal integrity improved dramatically. I realized I had been thinking like a student, not an engineer. Real engineering involves iteration, trial and error. When the 3D-printed prototype finally came together, I watched as my board powered up under the telescope mount.

welcome: It was good to talk on Wednesday morning your time.
_welcomeNote: Two facts a form letter cannot hold: WHEN the consult happened, stated on the FAMILY's clock rather than ours, and WHO is speaking. Derive the day from the consult's own timestamp in the family's timezone, never from the date it sits in our calendar; for a family far enough east these are different days. The test for this slot is whether the sentence could appear unchanged on another family's page; a date and a name cannot. Never let it grow into a description of the page itself, which is the deck-paragraph tic removed on 2026-09-03.
_headingNote: Shortened 2026-09-04 (Aaron: cut each hero so it does not wrap). Was 'Pick a time for the second conversation.', 'What happens in that conversation.' and 'The distance changes the calendar, not the counseling.' The international one is the only one that lost SENSE with its length: the pamphlet's 'not the counseling' half is the actual claim, and it now rests on the section body instead of the heading. Worth a look.
_escalationNote: Who moved this family off light, and when. `escalatedBy` is "family" (they wrote in and asked) or "ryan" (he decided to open the calendar for them); `escalatedAt` is the ISO stamp of that moment. Both null until it happens, and both are seeded like every other field, so either escalation path is one edit and one seed.
